ctx.x: Right. How would you contrast No Sun in Venice from Odds Against Tomorrow?

It was a different movie and a different theme and different music all together. Now Odds Against Tomorrow was Harry Belafonte. No Sun in Venice was like one of those gangster type melodramas, but Odds Against Tomorrow was a film with a purpose, as Belafonte always is in the forefront of equal rights and with Dr. King and all those things that he was involved with, demonstrations and what not. This movie was a breakthrough in the theme that the whole lesson to be learned from that film was that this great robbery…

a waiter, with the key to the getaway car. And the whole theme of the movie was finally when they were both blown up on the top of this gas tank at the end of the movie, the last line was when the coroner and these police were standing there trying to decide who was who and they were both charred, and he said something about, “Take your pick.” In other words…
